title: Karen Explodes After Police Deny Her Complaint
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

This suspect, Sharon, was charged with felony battery on a law enforcement officer and felony resisting with violence. She was later assigned a public defender to represent her in this case. However, that attorney filed a motion to raise the topic of incompetency to stand trial. The latest reports on the case indicate that after evaluation, a judge deemed she was incompetent to stand trial. While the case is still ongoing, she is being held at a state facility, and she is presumed innocent and less proven guilty in a court of law. Some people treat the police like it's a game that you can respond in. Like you can resist, throw a tantrum, and just hit restart. But in real life, there's no reset button, only consequences. And the crazy part is she's trying to get something handled while she's acting disorderly, loud and combative, which is like demanding help while you're lighting a room on fire. It's counterproductive and it's exactly why cops stop taking the same complaint over and over because some people don't want resolution, they just want to stay in charge. You don't get to treat the law like it's optional, like it's something you can argue down or just outsmart in the moment. Then turn around and try to play a victim when those same consequences grab you by the collar. I've seen people actually break down in the backseat of my cruiser, but the law doesn't negotiate and enforces. Problem is, the moment you learn that, it's usually too late.
